graphEvents.label: The sender is never told the lookup exists
The scorecard can report a pass that did not happen
Three root causes: note as only channel, readers and scorecard disagree, no per-runtime settings contract

label: Mode A: the sender is never told the lookup exists, so it writes a closing sentence instead of a pointer.
Mode B: the note outranks the lookup in the claim text because the offer prints after the note body with a weaker directive.
Mode C: a withheld offer is indistinguishable from no need to look because the mint returns null and the call site catches silently.
Mode D: the OpenCode reader can return another project's session when the store has no directory column.
Mode E: a secret survives redaction under x-api-key, inside an array under a secret key, or inside an image block.
Mode F: a detail past character 160 is invisible until the receiver loads the turn.
Mode G: model and effort do not carry on OpenCode because no branch reads or writes them and the root command has no model flag.
Mode H: a bare AI_SESSION_CHILD read suppresses the nudge in test sandboxes, and Pi and OpenCode keep in-process state so two hooks can both nudge.
Mode I: a claimed note never expires and the hold guard covers only question tools, so a prose ask leaves the sender's task open.
Mode J: the scorecard can report a pass that did not happen because the Pi pane has no marker and the harness has no token plant.
